description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). ## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

# 4.3b Inspector — the Clip tab's sections: video, audio, text and shape

The tab strip, the Clip tab's sub-tabs, pinned block, row marks and Reset/Clear are §4.3a; the Media, Document and Assistant tabs are §4.3c.

The section groups below are named as they were when each was a tab; they
are now sections of the Clip tab, offered when the selection has that aspect
  lands on the base props even inside an action, since motion is not an
  animation target. Also
  Clip ▸ Motion ▸; the timeline's name strip draws the in/out wedges and a
  During glyph. A stored zero-duration In or Out stays selected and editable
  but is explicitly marked inactive in the summary, selection note and menu;
  it draws no wedge (E2-27, §11).

**Audio sections** — clips whose audio is enabled and whose media has an
audio track, or nest clips with audio properties (`InspectorTab.hasAudio`).

- Volume % (the field 0–3200, the slider 0–400 with the knob pinned at its
  end above that; dB shown; §11 AU-1); **Loudness**, a read-out of the clip's
  integrated loudness and true peak over the window that plays at volume 1,
  nested object merges key by key (§5.2, §6), so an agent may send `gradient`
  with one key in it and keep the rest — and a `stops` LIST it sends replaces
  the whole list, which is why the row's Add and Remove re-send every stop.
- M3: *Spotlight* — which darkens the canvas outside a rectangle or
  ellipse, with an optional 1–2× zoom of the region (1 is none) — is a
  `video.spotlight` prop and appears in the **Picture** sub-tab, not here.

section's strips and fields write the same ranges, whole; Pick from Canvas's
pick is one `set_video`; `blur` 0–1 softens the weight by a Gaussian (GR-35), its Blur row the same key.

**A fifth part of the startup parity check holds that identity up**
(`AgentServer+Parity.swift`, road map 7's D3·5). For every op tool the
declared argument names must be exactly the core's for that op, plus the
injected `project` and `scope`, plus whatever a declarations row names, less
an argument a row says the app fills — in
both directions, so an argument the core has that no tool declares and an
argument a tool declares that no op has are each named with the op, the
argument and the side, and a declarations row naming an argument the core has
not got is named as stale. Because the catalog prints STRUCTURE and writes
only PROSE, the same part also complains about an argument that would reach an
agent with no description at all, and about a description written for an
argument the table has never heard of, which is how a misspelt prose key is
caught rather than dropped in silence. App-state tools are skipped by the same rule
part 4 uses — the core's own op list, which has no row for a tool with no op
behind it. What no comparison of two lists can see is a
CALL. A call's KEYS are compared to the tool's published schema at the
dispatch — the argument gate, kpgalligan/framejob#21, for all one hundred and four
product tools — so a name no tool published is refused naming the tool and what it
takes, where it used to be dropped in silence; and that an argument the
catalog prints is one a hand-written handler really reads is put to the
running binary by `tools/proof/op_argument_proof.py`, one left-out argument
per op.

The scope is read ONCE per call, at the dispatch, and an op with no `scope`
of its own follows the nest the app has OPEN — a call and the window agree
about which
container they mean, or `get_project` would list clips the very next op could
not name. An EXPLICIT scope outranks the open view. Plus
`set_scope {nest?, clip?}` (the mirror of the double-click and Clip ▸ Open
Nest, and what lets `render_frame` and `get_project` look inside a nest at
all; `clip` is the precise spelling, since a nest may be shown by two clips
at two different starts, and neither argument means the timeline),
`open_project {path}`, `new_project {path?}`, `import_media {path}` →
media id (a `.cube` LUT, §11 GR-8, answers kind `lut` and a note naming
`set_video {clips, patch: {look: {kind: "lut", media: N}}}`, and `add_media`'s
descriptor defaults `has_video` true only for a video or an image), `save_project` (it and `new_project {path}` refuse a path another
open project holds, naming that project, §11 #40), `close_project {discard?}`
(File ▸ Close, §11 #40: refused while a sheet is open on the window, and
with unsaved changes unless `discard: true`; it writes nothing, and a later
call naming the closed path is refused), `get_project` → the JSON, `set_playhead`,
`set_range`, `set_selection` and `undo` / `redo` (the view state and the
history are app state, not ops, but without a setter for each the "one
edit is one undo step" and "the in/out range scopes the export" properties
cannot be checked by driving the built app),
`import_captions {path, track?}` and `consolidate_media {}` (M3's two
§5.6 file features). The op tool `set_media_color {media, color}` (§11
GR-16, the ninety-first product tool) mirrors the Media tab's Camera Log
popup: `color` reaches the core unread (`setMediaColorRaw`), which answers
every refusal in its own sentence, and an absent `color` is the one thing
the handler names; `get_project`'s `media[].color` shows what import
detected. Copying a clip carries its media's Camera Log LUT row with it, so a
paste lands the conversion remapped. The op tool `set_media_speech {media,
spans}` (§11 AU-110, the hundred-and-fourth product tool) is the spans Duck by
Speech saves on a media: `spans` reaches the core unread. `set_audio` reads
one key of its patch, `duck.mode`: `speech` prepends `DuckSpeech.ops` — a
`set_media_speech` for each media without spans, from its voice cache — in
the same undo step, and its refusal (not a media clip with sound; speech not
detected yet) is the tool's error (AU-111).
For `transcribe(engine: "assemblyai")`, the handler validates typed arguments
and the target before the coordinator decides whether a keyless run can reuse
every packaged transcript. Keyless calls resolve no endpoint; a mixed or stale
batch is refused as a whole with no request or edit. Successful placement is
one grouped undo step, and `place: false` only returns cues. Deferred remote
deletions are named in `note` on success and in the error on failure.

`record_screen` (File ▸ New Recording…'s mirror) is §7.9d.

  reply. The trial is a one-off judgment and is not a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`; a check it
  leaves that should be repeated before releases becomes a JOB row citing "Source: the creator-jobs
  trial, T1/T2" (the grading trial's precedent, `docs/manual-checks.md:846–856`). Risk accepted: the
  trial may reorder the road map.
- **CJ-6 — The build arrangement.** The integration worktree `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs`,
  branch `worktree-creator-jobs`, from main. Each phase is one litecode pipeline (design → adversary
  → implement → review → fix) in a lane worktree, gated (`make gate`) and committed there, rebased
  onto the integration branch by one serialized integrator one landing at a time, and gated again.
  At most three lanes; a lane never builds against another lane's unlanded phase. At each landing
  the integrator renumbers what collides: a format bump (provisional from 38) with its
  `schema_vN.rs` and `format_history.rs` paragraph, decision IDs only when two phases claimed one,
  JOB numbers inside their block, screen numbers, and every count of CJ-8 (g). Merging into main
  follows CJ0a's question 1.
- **CJ-7 — IDs and records.** Phases are `XXn` (TX, CU, VR, FC, SW, CO, CJ); a split phase is
  `XXna`, `XXnb`…, sharing its block; a lettered phase split again takes a digit (`CU3a1`, `CU3a2`),
  its letter alone naming both halves. Phase XXn's decisions are XX-n0…XX-n9; XX0's are XX-1…XX-9; a
  bet with no zero phase records its scope-level decisions here under its own prefix (VR-1…VR-7,
  TX-70; SW-3 is in SW0's block). Spikes are XX-S1, XX-S2…; each rule is fixed in this file before
  its run, and each run's `results.json` stores as `rule_sha256` the SHA-256 of that spike's entry
  in "Every spike, with its rule" (from its bold ID to the line before the next entry), so records
  added elsewhere in this file leave it unchanged. A spike runs at the head of the first phase that
  uses it, in that phase's lane. Manual checks are `JOB-n` in blocks of ten: CJ 1–9, TX 10–19, CU
  20–29, VR 30–39, FC 40–49, SW 50–59, CO 60–69; a bet that needs more takes the next free block
  from 70. Handoffs are `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-<phase id lowercased>`. This file holds each
  phase's record.
- **CJ-8 — Shared reservations, so lanes do not collide.**
  - (a) The fifth inspector tab is TX's Transcript. Another tab, or a panel beside the inspector,
    needs a decision of its own (`InspectorViewController.swift` is frozen; five titles at the 280
    pt minimum are 56 pt each).
  - (b) The layer pass's `texture(4)` is CO's layer mask and `texture(5)` CU's cursor sprite.
    `LayerUniforms` groups of four are appended in landing order, and the integrator re-pins every
    proof that names the block's size.
  - (c) Every analysis kind of every bet lives in CJ2a's store under `cache/analysis/<kind>/` and
    runs on CJ2a's lane: `shots` and `faces` (CJ), `subjects` (VR), `masks` and `masks_best` (CO),
    `sound_events` (FC). No bet adds a sibling folder or a lane for analysis. Kind names use
    underscores.
  - (d) The road map's tools join dispatch through `AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift`:
    `creatorHandlers` and `creatorOffMainTools`, merged into the frozen file's `handlers` and
    `offMainTools` by its two existing lines (CJ0c's T8). Only an `opsWithoutTools` entry goes in
    the frozen file, as one line of wiring with its reason (CJ5a's `keep_range`). Dev tools join
    through `AgentServer+DevTools.swift`.
  - (e) A phase that adds a key equivalent records it, and the integrator checks
    `docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md` for a clash before landing.
  - (f) A bet's command is a composite over ops landing as one undo step through
    `performGroupedEdit`, and its tool runs the same planner (SY-1's shape), unless its rule must
    hold inside the core, in which case it is an op.
  - (g) The pinned counts a new tool or op moves — `OP_COUNT`, `PRODUCT_TOOLS`, `OPS`, `TOOLS`,
    `APP_STATE_TOOLS`, root `CLAUDE.md`'s "one hundred and six product tools", `app/CLAUDE.md`'s
    "sixty-four op tools", `documentLevelNames` (nine today: `refused_inside`'s ten less
    `add_adjustment_clip`) with `app/CLAUDE.md`'s stale "eight", `scope.rs:172`'s "fifty-three"
    (the ops that work inside a nest: `OP_COUNT` less `refused_inside`'s arms, 64 − 10 = fifty-four
    today, plus whatever the road map adds), spec §6a's "Ten ops", the dev tools' count in
    `dev_tools.py`, the catalog snapshot, `recording_probe.py`'s last-names assertion, and the
    assistant's tool lists (F4) — are edited by the phase that moves them, listed in its Docs and
    Acceptance, and renumbered by the integrator when two lanes move one.
  - (h) One composition-plan options export, `rc_project_composition_plan_opts(const RcProject *p,
    const char *opts_json)`, memoised per handle and options string: SW9a builds it (option
    `show_tracks`), VR7b adds `framing`. Without options the plan is byte-identical to
    `rc_composition_plan`'s.
  - (i) One action classifier, `core/src/action_class.rs` (`is_zoom`, `is_layout`, `moves`):
    whichever of CU7 and CO6 lands first creates it; the other reuses it. Actions carry no tag
    (CU-5, CO-63).
  - (j) One phrase splitter: TX7 builds it, pure and parameterised (sentence punctuation, a pause on
    the voice grid, a change of clip, track or speaker); FC4's `ClipSentences` calls it with FC-41's
    parameters.
  - (k) One dev hold for analysis, `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (CJ2a), and one canned-analysis switch,
    `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES` (CJ-26); VR and CO use them and add no hold of their own.
  - (l) `ReelCore.swift`'s room: the ledger in "Files at or near the cap", and question 6's answer.
- **CJ-9 — The clip ceiling is decided by spike CJ-S1 at CJ6's head.** Its verdict amends this
  entry: `MAX_CLIPS` stays 4,096 and TX and SW design around it (both read `RC_MAX_CLIPS`, so
  nothing spells 4,096), or CJ6 raises it to the spike's N.

**Scope-level decisions of the bets, recorded at CJ0a (their phases' sections hold the rest).**

- **VR-1 — Auto-reframe is in, as analysis plus ordinary actions.** Subjects are found offline by
  Vision's rectangle and saliency requests on the Mac and cached in CJ2a's store; the core plans the
  framing, and the result is placement and actions on the clip. No mask, no shipped model, no pixel
  work outside the one-pass compositor.
- **VR-2 — Bet 3 needs no key.** No VR control is disabled for a missing key.
- **VR-3 — A regenerated copy first; linked versions after it, on the owner's yes (CJ0a's
  question 8).** The planner answers a framing path, a similarity per instant from the source
  canvas to the target; the copy composes it into each clip, and linked versions store it per
  framing (VR7a–VR9). With a no, or a yes the vertical trial withdraws, VR7a–VR9 are filed as one
  issue carrying their design.
- **VR-4 — Subjects are boxes, detected per sample, never tracked by Vision.** Faces come from CJ3's
  `faces`; people (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2, `upperBodyOnly` false) and salient regions
  (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2) from VR1's `subjects`. A fresh
  `VNImageRequestHandler` per sample; no `VNTrackObjectRequest` or other stateful request. Linking
  boxes across samples is the core planner's (CJ-31); masks are out for framing (E9: they flicker).
- **VR-5 — The planner is the core's, and `reframe_clip` is an op (CJ-8 (f)).** Swift measures and
  caches; the core maps samples into clip time, chooses subjects, plans, enforces coverage and
  writes actions, because coverage (VR-7) needs (★) and `fill_scale` and composition into existing
  action ends needs the actions' own evaluation. The op is a pure function of the project and the
  samples handed to it.
- **VR-6 — No nest is made to make room for framing.** Framing is composed into the clip's own base
  and actions; a nest would cost tracks against `MAX_TRACKS` and wall the clip off from blurred
  backgrounds, filler cuts and the transcript.
- **VR-7 — A followed picture never shows the canvas, with three named exceptions.** The window lies
  inside the clip's picture (scale at least fill, offsets clamped by (★)), every key is a covering
  state, and one curve carries x, y and scale, so every frame between keys covers too (the covering
  placements are convex). Exceptions: **`fit` spans** (the whole picture, the canvas around it,
  unless `backdrop` puts a blurred copy behind; a nest clip has none); **motion** (a `video.motion`
  that moves or turns the layer keeps its motion, and the guarantee excludes its span — the whole
  clip for a During motion; `spin` counts as rotation; `fade` is not an exception); **opacity**
  (fades, transitions and opacity below 1 are the author's).
- **TX-70 — A review pass may strike a phrase the speaker said again, found by comparing the spelled
  words of neighbouring phrases; it offers every strike for review and cuts nothing until the person
  removes it. Amends TR-3, AI-6 and W-9** (the orchestrator's reading of the owner's "Add all: 1-6",
  2026-11-01: bet 1 as the survey wrote it carries survey decision 3's amendment; CJ0a's question 7
  confirms it). It finds a **restart** (a phrase whose words are the opening words of the next), a
  **retake** (a phrase of four or more words most of whose words recur, in order, at the start of
  one of the next few phrases, TX-71's numbers) and a **repeat** (one to four words said twice in a
  row); the earlier is struck, the last kept. It reads each word's text lowercased with edge
  punctuation trimmed (TR-8's rule, fillers left out), their order, the pauses between them (the
  voice cache) and sentence punctuation; phrases are compared only within one track and, where
  labels exist, one speaker; one take placed twice (the same media's same source ticks) is never a
  retake. No model reads the words, nothing is sent, no key is needed. A false start that repeats no
  words stays the assistant's, on the person's ask (TR-5). Amending lines: **TR-3** "a false start
  that repeats words — a restart, or a line said again — is found by TX-70's comparison of spelled
  words and offered struck for review; one that repeats no words is found only by reading what was
  meant, so no pipeline does it (W-9, AI-6); the assistant may, when the person asks (TR-5)";
  **AI-6** "a pipeline may strike words for review by comparing their spelling, order and timing
  with the phrases beside them; that is not picking words by meaning, and nothing is cut until the
  person removes the strikes"; **W-9** "the Transcript tab's review pass strikes repeated phrases
  for the person to remove, by comparing spelled words, never by a language model; captions are
  untouched". Risk accepted: a deliberate repetition is struck and shown for review.
- **SW-3 — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera clips (angles) stay
  whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip copied from an
  angle at the same time. Switch by Speaker writes the program track, Switch Angle re-picks a shot,
  and the Angle Viewer shows every angle and switches while playing. There is no multicam source
  kind and no nest in point: every shot can be rolled, trimmed, graded and deleted like any clip,
  and spec §2's one kind of track holds.

| G-1 | "**Amended by CJ-1** (2026-11-01): §1's clause 'nothing else is scriptable' is lifted with the plugin non-goal. A graphic stays a source and nothing else becomes scriptable until a road map decides it in writing." |
| R5-1 | "**Noted by CJ-1** (2026-11-01): the plugin non-goal is lifted; effects stay closed vocabularies until a road map amends this entry." |
| GR-1 | "**Noted by CJ-1** (2026-11-01): §1 no longer lists grading as a non-goal." |

section (CJ1's R6-17, AI-8 and TR-10; TX's TR-14, TR-11, AI-4, AI-14; CU's `recording.md`, CAM-4,
CAM-9; and so on).

# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.
   Text / Shape for the selected clip; Media and Document always.
6. **A small keyboard vocabulary.** ⌘T split, W/E trim to playhead,
   ⌘⌫ ripple delete, ⇧⌘F freeze frame, M marker, Space/JKL transport.

Left out: everything that only makes sense for a recording
it made itself (mouse/keyboard/touch callouts, pointer effects), templates,
publishing to YouTube/Vimeo, the stock-media library.

- **GR-1 — The grading experiment: tier 1 is IN, kept by the owner's verdict; tiers 2 and 3 are filed as issues.** Tier 1 is tone, adjustment clips, looks and `.cube` LUT import, with a way to see the
  grade: a before/after switch (View ▸ Show Ungraded, preview only) and one luma waveform. Flip and
  the shape mask leave the experiment (flip touches nothing about colour; a matte track over an
  adjustment clip does the mask's job). Wheels, curves, qualifiers, further scopes and the rest of
  tiers 2 and 3 are not OUT: they wait for the owner's verdict at GR7 (`archive/grading.md`, "Worth
  keeping"). **Amends spec §1**: its non-goal "color grading beyond per-clip controls" and the bar
----
- **W-9 — No language model chooses words.** Keyword emphasis and emoji
  insertion are left out: every styled word is styled by its position in
  time, never by its meaning (road map 8 §4 W-9).
  **Amended 2026-09-27, by AI-6 (road map 12): W-9 governs automatic
  styling, not a person's request.** No PIPELINE picks words by meaning.
  The assistant writes a caption's text or style only because the person
  asked it to in the conversation, and each such edit is an ordinary undo
  step.
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-5:** the assistant may also choose words to
  CUT by their meaning (a false start) when the person asks, reading them
  through `get_transcript`; no pipeline does.
- **W-10 (the core's sentence) — `set_text` can patch `case`, `words` and
  `word_style`,** because deepening D1 makes every declared key patchable.
  That is the agent's door, and it is not a promise that a hand-restyled
  page still fits: restyling is regenerating (road map 8 §4 W-10).
- **W-11 — Three style choices are confirmed as shipped** (the user,
  2026-09-28, closing #45): Karaoke is the one style that pages to two
  lines (every other style is one row); the caption faces bundled are
  Montserrat ExtraBold and Black, Anton and Bebas Neue (OFL, in
----
- **TR-3 — Two paths, split by who judges: fillers are deterministic, and false starts are a
  judgement of meaning.** The owner's decision 2.
  - A filler is a word in a closed vocabulary, found by its spelling and cut on its own timing:
    no judgement of meaning, so a pipeline may do it (TR-4).
  - A false start ("I was — we were going") is found only by reading what was meant, so no
    pipeline does it (W-9, AI-6); the assistant may, when the person asks (TR-5).
  - Risk accepted: a filler the vocabulary does not spell, or one the engine did not report, is
    not offered; a false start is never offered without a conversation.
- **TR-4 — Remove Filler Words… is shaped like Remove Silences: a sheet, a candidate wash on the
  timeline, one `ripple_delete_ranges` undo step, and its own read-half MCP tool,
  `detect_fillers`.** The owner's decision 2, its first sub-point.
  - **The pieces:** `detect_fillers` answers the ranges and cuts nothing, as `detect_silence`

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

# Objections

## 1
- **Risk category:** under-scope
- **Claim:** The §11 index edits cover the decision rows and the file rows for `recording.md` and `camera-recording.md`. They do not cover three other FILE rows that still describe lifted exclusions as in force. That breaks the spec's own Constraints rule that "no row there may still state a lifted exclusion as in force" (01-spec.md:52).
- **Evidence:** `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md:33` (grading-3 file row: "GR-20: a wide-gamut working space for SDR projects closed as not wanted"), `:34` (grading-4 file row: "GR-27: an Offset wheel closed as not wanted; GR-28 … GR-29 … GR-30 …"), `:47` (audio file row: "AU-2: §1's audio non-goal lifted (…; third-party plug-in hosting stays out …"). None of :33, :34 or :47 is in the Interfaces "§11 index rows" list (01-spec.md:34) or in the road map's bullet 4 (creator-jobs.md, CJ0a "Spec edits").
- **Suggested change:** Add the file rows :33, :34 and :47 to the Interfaces list. Each gets the same qualifier as its decision rows: "— not excluded since CJ-1; not built" for GR-20 and GR-27…GR-30, and AU-2's "the plugin non-goal lifted by CJ-1; the decision stands as current design".

## 2
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** The spec changes CJ-7's `rule_sha256` byte range only in the new §11 file. The road map's own CJ-7 text keeps the old range, "from its bold ID to the line before the next entry". The spike section points readers at that text ("`rule_sha256` (CJ-7)"). For the last entry of every group, the old range takes in the blank lines and the group heading that follow. So a spike phase that hashes by the road map gets a different value from the table CJ0a records.
- **Evidence:** `designs/creator-jobs.md:806–807` has the old definition, and Approach 2 does not edit it (only CJ-8 (l) at :855 is replaced in the draft list). `designs/creator-jobs.md:1035` cites CJ-7 for `rule_sha256`.
